aiSummary: Choctawhatchee Bay is fishing well this Sunday morning, with speckled trout leading the inshore bite across grass flats and bull redfish showing up strong near structure — both species are responding best to early outings before the heat index climbs toward 105°F. A 24% storm chance with a window before 1 PM means you have a solid morning window, especially on the falling tide that sets up around 3:27 PM; plan to be off exposed water by midday. Water temp is holding at 85°F with slightly stained clarity, so lean toward louder or chartreuse presentations to help fish locate your bait.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans a narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel that pushes bait through on both tides and concentrates speckled trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum around the pilings year-round. The lee-side pilings are the prime ambush zone, particularly on incoming tides when fish stack up to intercept passing bait. Keep in mind this is open, exposed water — it's typically the first spot to become unfishable when wind builds or weather moves through.
bridge.todaysCall: The near-slack incoming tide early this morning transitions to a long falling tide bottoming out around 3:27 PM, so the moving water through the bridge funnel will be most productive in those mid-morning falling-tide hours. Light westerly winds at 5–10 mph will create a manageable chop on this exposed water, but keep a close eye on conditions as the storm window opens before 1 PM — this is the first spot you'll want to leave if skies build. Work the lee-side pilings hard with soft plastics or live shrimp; the near-full moon's spring-tide push means stronger-than-average current through the funnel, which should stack bait and predators together. Slightly stained water favors darker or chartreuse plastics to help trout and reds zero in on your presentation. Aim to be fishing by first light and wrap up well before noon given the storm risk.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers well-protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, plus trout and flounder at the mouth — the oyster bars at the creek entrance are the prime target zone. Tree cover keeps water temperatures a few degrees cooler than the open bay and provides meaningful shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions toward brackish conditions and can produce bass alongside smaller redfish.
alaqua.todaysCall: This is a smart choice today given the heat index pushing toward 105°F — the tree-lined banks offer real shade and the protected nature of the bayou keeps chop manageable even with west winds at 5–10 mph. Fish the oyster bars at the mouth during the falling tide this afternoon, but the better play today is an early morning session before the storm window opens before 1 PM. Bay-wide reports confirm reds are showing up strong, and Alaqua's year-round redfish population should be active in the slightly stained water — try weedless gold spoons or dark soft plastics along the oyster bar edges. The near-full waxing gibbous moon is driving a strong tidal push, so expect more pronounced water movement through the creek mouth than a typical neap tide, which will concentrate bait and fish on the bars. Get in early, work the shade, and plan your exit ahead of the midday storm window.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees notably less fishing pressure than nearby Alaqua and LaGrange, which tends to mean less-educated fish and better reaction strikes. The interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano occasionally show at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It is somewhat less protected than LaGrange when weather builds, so factor that in on unsettled days.
basin.todaysCall: The lighter pressure here makes Basin Bayou worth the trip on a Sunday when other spots may see more boat traffic, and the interior grass flats are ideal for sight-fishing reds in the early morning light before heat and glare become a factor. With water temp at 85°F, fish will be most active in the first two to three hours after sunrise at 5:58 AM — get shallow and look for tailing or cruising reds on the flat before the sun gets high. The spring-tide push from the near-full moon will move water meaningfully across these shallow flats, helping push baitfish up and triggering feeding activity. Slightly stained water reduces sight-fishing visibility somewhat, so polarized lenses are a must and you may need to rely more on popping corks or noisy topwaters to draw strikes. Be mindful that Basin offers less weather protection than LaGrange — with a 24% storm chance before 1 PM, commit to an early-morning window and don't push your luck into the afternoon.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is considered the top trout producer among the bayous on this side of the bay, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside the bayou hold black drum and sheepshead, rounding out a diverse fishery. It is the most protected water on this side of the bay, making it the default choice when weather is building or conditions deteriorate elsewhere.
lagrange.todaysCall: LaGrange is the right call today for anglers who want premium protection if that pre-1 PM storm window materializes — you can stay productive and stay safe without having to run back to the ramp. Start on the oyster bar mouth during the early falling tide phase and work soft plastics or live shrimp across the bar edges; bay-wide reports show trout as the standout bite right now and these bars are as good a trout address as exists on the bay. The strong tidal push from the near-full moon will create above-average current flow across the bars, which is exactly the kind of feeding trigger that stacks trout and reds on ambush points. Slightly stained water calls for chartreuse, root beer, or dark-bodied plastics rather than natural-match patterns. If afternoon storms do roll through, you can retreat deeper into the bayou's interior and target black drum or sheepshead around the deep holes while waiting out the weather — this spot gives you options.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a short tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, making it one of the most convenient and protected fisheries on this part of the bay. Tidal flow pushes baitfish up the creek on incoming tides, concentrating redfish and trout in the bends and along grass edges. The creek mouth is a prime flounder zone, and the upper section transitions toward brackish water that holds bass alongside smaller reds.
fourmile.todaysCall: With the storm window before 1 PM and heat index approaching 105°F, Four Mile Creek's short run time and protected character make it an excellent default for today — you're never far from the ramp if conditions go sideways fast. The long falling tide running from now through the 3:27 PM low will push baitfish back toward the creek mouth, concentrating reds and trout in the bends through the mid-morning hours; fish the inside turns of each bend with paddle-tail soft plastics or live shrimp. The creek mouth is worth working for flounder, which the bay-wide report confirms are a regular bycatch on flat edges and sandy channels this time of year — drag a slow-rolled plastic or live finger mullet along the bottom at the transition zone. Slightly stained water here shouldn't be a major issue in the tight confines of the creek where fish are keying on current and structure rather than open-water sight-feeding. This is as close to a no-excuses, all-conditions option as the dashboard offers today.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide destination and one of the most consistently productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay. Summer mornings are peak season, with trout stacked on grass in two to four feet of water, and Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides. The bayou sees regular angler pressure but continues to produce reliably — factor in the longer run time from the 331 Bridge area.
hogtown.todaysCall: This is the spot that aligns most directly with the bay-wide bite report — the Santa Rosa Beach guide notes in recent reports are almost certainly referencing Hogtown Bayou and surrounding flats, making this a high-confidence pick for trout right now. Hit the grass flats in two to four feet of water as early as possible after the 5:58 AM sunrise; the near-full moon's spring tide will be moving water across the flats even as the tide shifts to falling, which keeps trout actively feeding rather than sulking in deep holes. Slightly stained water means topwaters and louder subsurface presentations — popping corks with shrimp or paddle-tails in chartreuse or dark colors — will outperform finesse or natural-match rigs today. Check the mouth for Spanish mackerel on the moving water before heading to the flats; they tend to show when current is running and bait is concentrated. Factor in the longer run time from Shipyard Marina and make sure you're set up and fishing well before the pre-1 PM storm window — Hogtown is worth the run, but not if you're arriving as weather builds.

rocky.aiNote: Rocky Bayou sits inside Fred Gannon Rocky Bayou State Park near Niceville, offering a protected, scenic, and significantly less-pressured fishery compared to bayous closer to the 331 Bridge. Freshwater influence from Rocky Creek makes it an excellent flounder destination, and the glass-calm state park coves are well suited to sight-fishing redfish. Mangrove snapper hold near dock pilings, and the bayou is the furthest location from Shipyard Marina on this dashboard.
rocky.todaysCall: Rocky Bayou's state park setting means light Sunday pressure even on a summer weekend, and the protected coves will stay calm and fishable even if the westerly breeze ticks up toward the higher end of the 5–10 mph forecast. The freshwater influence keeps water temperatures marginally cooler than the open bay, which matters on a day where surface temps are sitting at 85°F — target the upper sections of the bayou early for reds and flounder before heat pushes fish deeper or tighter to shade. Work the glass-calm coves for sight-fishing reds on the falling tide as water clarity, though slightly stained, is relatively better in the shaded, low-traffic environment here. Mangrove snapper around dock pilings are a reliable bonus target on any tide; drop a small jig or live shrimp tight to structure for a quick hit. The significant run time from Shipyard Marina is today's main logistical consideration — leave early enough to fish the prime morning window and still be headed home well before the pre-1 PM storm chance arrives.
